overall.summary: All tools are implemented as described and no declared effects are missing; the mismatches are that every tool silently performs symlink resolution and allow-list validation via validatePath (with process.chdir anchoring and inode identity checks for writes), applies a 15-second filesystem-call timeout, blocks on a roots-refresh barrier, and returns a special error block when no allowed directories exist on a modern-era connection — none of which is mentioned in any tool description. Additionally, the server dynamically replaces its allowed-directory list at runtime from MCP client Roots, so list_allowed_directories may return directories different from those provided at startup.

startup.behaviour: Resolves command-line directory arguments with fs.realpath (via realpathWithRetry), storing both the original normalized path and the realpath when they differ (e.g. macOS /tmp → /private/tmp)
Warns to stderr and skips directories that are not accessible or not directories; exits with code 1 if all specified directories are inaccessible
Prints 'Secure MCP Filesystem Server running on stdio' to stderr at startup

After initialize handshake (2025-era clients), fetches MCP roots via server.listRoots() and replaces allowed directories with validated roots; if client has no roots capability and no command-line directories, closes the connection and calls onCannotOperate (process.exit(1))

Installs a notification handler for 'notifications/roots/list_changed' that fetches updated roots and replaces the allowed directory list at runtime; installs a barrier so in-flight tool calls wait for the updated roots
Reads package.json from disk at module load time to determine the SERVER_VERSION string reported in serverInfo
